title: snapshot: skip building a part whose inputs have not changed
lead: With `--since`, slicer still loads each project and builds each part before it can say `unchanged`, because a part's revision is a hash of its built value. A cheap fingerprint of the files a part reads would let slicer answer before the load, which is the time ork's polling spends. This is a row with an open question; it needs the owner's answers before it is specified.
findings_note: Follow-up the owner chose on 2026-11-11 while specifying the snapshot deps/--since item: --since drops an unchanged part's value but still loads the store and builds it, because a revision is a hash of the value.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/snapshot.py:14-15` and `:73`: the revision is computed from the built value, so it cannot be known before the store is loaded.
- Measured 2026-11-11: `slicer snapshot --json` takes 129 ms on this repository, against 80 ms for `--version`; the difference is the store load and the part builds.

Open owner questions:

- Q1 the fingerprint. (a) a new `fingerprint` beside `revision`, a hash of `(path, mtime_ns, size)` for each file the part reads (`.slicer/index.json`, `.slicer/slices/`, the relay-run ledger, config), checked before the load; `revision` keeps its meaning (recommended). (b) redefine `revision` as the fingerprint, which changes what existing callers compare.
- Q2 the fall-back when a part reads git state (`health` reads `vcs.merge_in_progress`): (a) such a part is always built (recommended). (b) include the git files it reads in the fingerprint.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: 1. Wait for the owner's answers to Q1 and Q2, then write the steps.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes.
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check` exits 0.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch.
